decisionsTitle: The review of «Planul voluntarilor» and the raffle, answered: an import keeps the plan at every point the file still has, «Participă la tombolă» travels with a person turned runner or volunteer, a refused press lands on its sentence, and the tick has a predicate of its own (amending §949, and with it §948 and §289)
decisionsSection:
**Why.** «Planul voluntarilor» and the raffle in the backoffice (§949) were built on 2026-11-16 and shipped the same day, on the owner's word, before the findings of their review were answered. That review — seven readers, one lens each, every finding above a nit checked by two more — found no blocker and left seventeen findings. This section answers all seventeen; each was checked against the code first, and each was true. The race is Saturday, 2026-11-21: the organizers build the plan on a phone this week.

### What is decided here

**1. An import over an event keeps the plan** (amending §949, which said «an import of the event's file that changes the points replaces them, and the plan with them»). The plan places a volunteer at a point by the point's row (`event_volunteers.checkpoint_id`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`), and the import (`replaceCheckpoints`) deleted every point of the event and inserted the file's whenever the two lists differed in anything — a note, a tick. So one imported file silently took every volunteer of the event off the plan, and the club moves events between QA and production with exactly these files. Now a point the file still has keeps its row:

- a file carries no ids (§751), so a point is known by what the file says of it — **the same Romanian name at the same kilometre**. That row is updated in place — the English name, what the point offers, its time limit, its note, its tick and its place in the list are the file's — as the editor's own save keeps a row (`changeCheckpoints`, §757), and the people standing at it stay;
- a point the file no longer has is deleted, and only its people stand under «Fără punct pe traseu» again; a point the file adds is inserted, with nobody;
- a point **renamed or moved** in the file is, to a file, another point: the old one leaves with its people freed. They are still the event's volunteers, with their roles, to be placed again;
- two points a file names alike are matched in the file's order, each to a row of its own and never both to one; a third is a new point.

Everything else the import does to the points is what it did: the list reads by distance with the file's values, a tie at one kilometre in the file's order, the places renumbered; the diff says the same words; and the trail holds the same one row (`event_checkpoints.changed`, `source: "import"`, the list before and after, counted as a whole list replaced). A kept row keeps its own `created_at`, which orders nothing once every row is renumbered. Nobody is told. `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` says, where it says what an import over an event changes, to open the plan after a file that renamed, moved or dropped a point.

**2. «Participă la tombolă» travels with the person** (amending §948 and §949). «Transformă în voluntar» and «Transformă în alergător» write a new row on the other list, and a new row starts in the raffle — the column's default. So a person an organizer had taken out was back on «Lista pentru tombolă» by a press that was about something else. Now a runner who was out is out as a volunteer, and the registration a volunteer becomes takes the volunteer's tick, whichever it is — the entry may restart a registration of that person cancelled earlier, and that row keeps what it once held. Each way through the tick's own writer (`changeVolunteer`'s `setRaffle`, `raffle-mark.ts#setRegistrationInRaffle`), in the transform's transaction and with that writer's audit row; a tick that is already right writes nothing. Neither the allocator nor the staff entry reads the column — the guard still holds them to that — which is why the transform says it and not the entry. §948's «nothing the person told the organizers as a volunteer is copied onto the registration» stands: the tick is the organizers' mark, no answer of the person's.

**3. The tick has a predicate of its own, `canSetRaffleMark`** (amending how §949 amended §289). §949 gave the Organizer one write on a registration and authorized it with `canReadRegistrations` — while `roles.ts` still said that predicate grants none. A later reader of that file would have been told the opposite of what the code did. The predicate is the readers' set, role for role — the Organizer, the Administrator, the Superadministrator — and is written as `canReadRegistrations`, so moving who reads the list moves who ticks and nobody ticks a registration they may not read; it is asked by `setRegistrationRaffleAction` at the door and by `setRegistrationInRaffle` again (BR-REQ-060-01), and by nothing else. **No role's power changed.** `canReadRegistrations` answers reading and authorizes no write.

**4. A refused press on the plan lands on its sentence.** «Pune aici» and «Scoate» came back to the point's anchor whatever happened. A refusal — the person cancelled meanwhile, the point taken off the route meanwhile, a role that may not — has its words in the alert at the top of the page, off the screen from a point further down, and a deleted point has no anchor left to land on. Now a press that went through comes back to its point and a refusal to `#admin-alert`, the registrations list's rule (§943); the alert region is focusable and stands clear of the page's top, as the other backoffice pages' regions do.

**5. The organizers' own marks expire no public cache.** `changeVolunteer` expired the public «places» rows after `setCheckpoint` and `setRaffle`, though no public page reads either: an expiry is a read that may wake the database (§333), and the plan is built one press a person on race week. Both are left out as «Are kit» already was (§904); every other change to a volunteer expires «places» as before.

**6. The telephone on the plan is the one the person's page draws.** It was the number as typed, in a small inline link. An organizer rings from the plan with a thumb on Saturday: it is read grouped — the country's code, then the rest in threes (`formatPhone`) — its `tel:` link holds the digits and the plus alone, and it is 44 pixels tall (BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 6). On paper it is the number as text — no link's colour, no underline, no height that would space the sheet.

**7. The words.** «Pus la punct» is an idiom in Romanian — to put somebody in their place — and a participle said of a person reads wrong for half of them. The toasts say «Stă la punctul ales: apare în planul voluntarilor.» and «Nu mai stă la niciun punct: e din nou la „Fără punct pe traseu”.»; the plan says «încă de confirmat» (it said «neconfirmat încă»), «Toată lumea stă la câte un punct.» and «Încă nu stau la niciun punct, sau au o treabă care nu ține de traseu…»; the column's hint «Gol: încă fără punct…»; a person's data «Nu participă la tombolă» (it said «Scos de la tombolă»); and the volunteers' «Tombolă» hint speaks of «persoana», as the registrations' does. The English follows where the sense moved.

**8. Who ticks «Avem tombolă».** §949 called it «the organizers' own switch». It is a box of the event editor, and the event's save is the Administrator's (§542): an Administrator ticks it, the Organizer reads it and works the column it shows. The schema, the editor's box and the fields now say so. The box's help, «Doar pentru organizatori: pe site nu apare nimic», stays: it is the house's phrase for «internal», of the people who see it, not of who saves.

**9. Smaller things.** «Punctele de pe traseu, în editorul evenimentului» opens the editor at the points' own card (`#box-checkpoints`) instead of its top. The comments that said only «an Administrator» takes a person out of the raffle name the Organizer too. In `admin/volunteers/actions.ts` each action has its own comment again. `docs/WHERE-THINGS-LIVE.md` names, on the plan's row and on the raffle's, the guard that holds «never public, no email, no badge, no file».

### What the review asked to be proven, and now is

- **No press of the plan or of the volunteers' raffle tick queues an email**, for people who have an address and a role: asserted on the outbox.
- **A series save does not carry «Avem tombolă»** to another date, «from this date» or to all of them: the code was right and had no test; it has one, the mirror of the kit's, which does travel.
- **Migration `0205`** on a database migrated by the release before it: every event from before holds no raffle, every registration and volunteer from before is in one.
- **The «Punct» and «Tombolă» columns** of the «Voluntari» list are read in English too.
- **The two guards** (`plan-never-leaves.test.ts`, `raffle-never-leaves.test.ts`) found a reader by the words it uses — a column's name, the module's path as the `@/` alias writes it — and so missed `./plan` and `../raffle-mark`, the import a file beside the module would write, the allocator's own file among them. They now resolve what a file imports against the file's own folder (`tests/helpers/module-imports.ts`), and each proves it on a fixture of its own.
- **The roles' table** has the new predicate for every role, and a test pins the two places that ask it and that nothing else does.

### Refused, and not done

**Refused: ids in the event's file.** They would say which point is which, but a file moves between environments whose rows have other ids, and the file's rule is that it carries none (§751).

**Refused: matching a point by its name alone, or by its kilometre alone.** Either keeps the people of a point that was only renamed or only moved — and either also keeps them at the wrong point when a file swaps two names, or puts a new point at an old kilometre, with nothing on the screen to say so. Both together is exact; what it costs is that a renamed point's people are placed again, which the plan shows at once under «Fără punct pe traseu».

**Not done.** An audit row naming each person freed when a point is deleted, in the editor or by an import: it needs its own decision. A line in the import's diff that says how many volunteers a changed point would free. The import's audit row still counts a whole list replaced, as it always did, though rows are now kept. The SPECS criteria that landed with §949 are not renumbered; the ones below amend them.
changelogLine: - **«Planul voluntarilor» survives an import** — importing an event's file over an event no longer takes everybody off the plan: people stay at every point the file still has (the same name at the same kilometre), and only those of a point the file renamed, moved or dropped are back under «Fără punct pe traseu», to be placed again. Somebody taken out of the raffle stays out when turned from runner into volunteer, or back. On the plan a refused press now lands on its message at the top of the page, the telephone number is a link a thumb can press, read grouped, and «Punctele de pe traseu» opens the editor at the points' own card. The words say «Stă la punctul ales», «încă de confirmat» and «Nu participă la tombolă» in place of the ones that read wrong. Who may do what is unchanged. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 229 in what frees a point's people. Given an event's file imported over an event whose points volunteers stand at, when the file's list of points differs from the event's, then every point the file still has — the same Romanian name at the same kilometre — keeps its row, takes the file's English name, kinds, time limit, note, profile tick and place in the list, and the volunteers standing at it stay; a point the file no longer has is removed and only its people stand at no point again; a point the file adds is added with nobody; a point renamed or moved in the file is another point; two points the file names alike are matched in the file's order, each to a row of its own and never both to one; afterwards the list reads by distance with the file's values, a tie at one kilometre in the file's order, an export of the event gives the file's points back, the trail holds one `event_checkpoints.changed` row with `source: "import"` naming the list before and after, and nobody is told; a file whose points are the event's own writes nothing to them (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 229 and 230 in where a press comes back to and what it tells. Given `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari`, when «Pune aici» or «Scoate» goes through — a press that finds the person already there included — then it comes back to the point it was made on (`#point-<id>`); when it is refused — the person cancelled meanwhile, the point taken off the route meanwhile, a role that may not — then it comes back to the page's alert region (`?planError=CODE#admin-alert`), which says the refusal's sentence, is focusable and stands clear of the page's top. The telephone number is read grouped in a `tel:` link of digits and the plus alone, 44 pixels tall (BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 6) and printed as text; the link to the points opens the event editor at «Puncte pe traseu». No press of the plan and no press of the volunteers' «Tombolă» tick queues an email, for a person with an address and a role, or expires a public cache, while every other change to a volunteer still expires the public «places» rows; and the «Punct» and «Tombolă» columns of the «Voluntari» list are said in English to an English reader (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 35 and 36, and BR-REQ-037-03 criterion 31, in what a transform carries. Given a registration whose «Participă la tombolă» was unticked, when an Administrator presses «Transformă în voluntar», then the volunteer entered is out of the raffle too, by the volunteers' own tick and its `volunteer.edited` row; given a volunteer whose tick was unticked, when an Administrator presses «Transformă în alergător», then the registration the entry wrote is out of the raffle too, by the registrations' own tick and its `registration.raffle_excluded` row — and where the entry restarted an earlier registration of that person, the row takes the volunteer's tick whichever it is; a person who was in stays in with nothing written; «Lista pentru tombolă» leaves out whoever was out before the press; nobody is told and nothing else of either row moves; and a series save, «from this date» or to every date, carries «Avem tombolă» to no other date (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 14 where it lists what the Organizer may not change on a registration. Given «Participă la tombolă» on a registration — the one write an Organizer makes there (`DECISIONS.md` §949) — then it is authorized by a predicate of its own, `canSetRaffleMark`, true exactly for the roles that read the registrations (the Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator; false for a member, the desk Volunteer, the Redactor and the Tehnic role), asserted at the door by `setRegistrationRaffleAction` and again by `setRegistrationInRaffle` and asked by nothing else; `canReadRegistrations` authorizes no write, and no role's power changed. Given «Avem tombolă» on an event, then it is saved with the event by an Administrator, and an Organizer's save of the event is refused (FORBIDDEN) with the box unchanged (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the review of «Planul voluntarilor» and the raffle, answered: an import keeps the plan, the raffle tick travels with a person, a refusal lands on its sentence
